subject: re-dif
title: RE.DEF.  ---- C.CONT.
description: Second diagram on page 295 (CMOA(II)-53), paired with the (R)RE-DOC × C-CONT crossing above it. Where the first diagram crosses redocumentation with composite-continuance, this one shows the same crossing one transformation deeper: (C)RE-DIF (the *concept* of redefinitions — the cycle in which the form's working definitions get rewritten) crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance). RE-DIF is subject on the left with the subject-arrow, drawn as (c)re.def.; the main line runs up-right to C-CONT, which has no branches of its own. Across the top, TRS (transition) rises from the main line, SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) branches from TRS to the left, and PROG-SIGN (progressional significance) hangs from SOC-RT-DY just above the subject — the same upper arrangement the previous diagram used. POL-DY (political dynamics) runs right from the main line, with RT-DY (reality dynamics) rising from it. Lower down, MT-IMP (multi-implications) runs right from the main line; MT-DI (multi-dimensional) drops from the MT-IMP line, DY-F (dynamic functionalism) branches from MT-DI to the bottom-left margin, and INFO-DY (information dynamics) branches from MT-DI to the right, with RE-ST (restructuralism) hanging from INFO-DY. Structural argument: redefinitions crossed with composite-continuance build their side structure from three points on the main line — transition, political-dynamics and multi-implications.
